nearest_prs.read: Body read: open a food can with a two-handle rotary opener; one hand keeps the handles squeezed while the other turns the key until the cut goes all the way round, then lays the opener down.
nearest_prs.comparison: Same object family (a food can and a hand opener) but the opposite end of the job and a different skill: theirs cuts the lid with a tool; ours starts after a cut that stopped short, with no opener in the scene, and is about folding the stiff, plastically bent hanging lid down into a light, tip-prone can held by the other hand before binning it. No cutting, no tool operation.

nearest_prs.read: Body read: retract a utility knife's blade with the slider before stowing the knife in a toolbox tray; stowing it blade-out or touching the blade scores 0.
nearest_prs.comparison: Same safety pattern (make a sharp edge safe before putting the item away, unprompted ordering latched at 0), different object and mechanism: a slider on a knife vs. bending a hinged tinplate flap past vertical and into a can. Reviewers may see the shared 'neutralise the sharp edge first' framing; the manipulation and the real-world setting (household recycling, sorter hazard) differ.

physical_skill: Notice, without being told, that an empty 50 g steel soup can's cut lid still hangs from the rim on an uncut tab, standing 10 degrees past vertical with its jagged edge up; hold the can with one gripper and with the other push the lid back over from outside (pressing from above opens it further) and on down into the can against the tab's ~0.08 N m yield moment until its free edge is at least 2 cm below the seam, then put the can in an open-top caddy and let go.

distinct_from_nearest: No accepted or live task folds a hanging can lid into its can before recycling. 1851 cuts a lid with an opener; 2481 drops a plain can through a pedal bin's lid; 672 retracts a knife blade. The task is distinct in object state (partially cut, plastically bent lid), skill (two-handed fold of a stiff flap into a light unstable container) and context (household recycling guidance from Calgary, Gresham, Logan; Metro and Rockhampton use cans as containers for small lids). Residual risks: a reviewer may group it with 672 as 'make the sharp thing safe first', and programmes that accept large lids loose (Metro, Rockhampton) make 'fold it in' one acceptable option rather than the only one; the README states this limit.
